rule_errors_confirmed: Described the 12-inch rim diameter as a 'wide, stable base' and 'a lip to grip' - unsupported functional and dimensional interpretations

assessment: The candidate's first-turn page was complete and well-structured, and the revision successfully converted vague fluff into concrete, mechanism-backed beginner benefits (steak sear, crispy chicken skin, stovetop-to-oven cooking) that directly answered the editorial feedback. However, the revision gained persuasive force through invented details - most notably mischaracterizing the 12-inch rim as a stable base and grip lip, plus unsupported capacity and longevity claims. The final output was only a partial section rather than the full assembled page, dropping care instructions, safety warnings, the lid exclusion, and the call to action. The result is a vivid but incomplete and partially distorted product page.
judge_agreement: All five judges agreed the revision made the copy more concrete and scannable, and that delivering only a section instead of the full page was a significant weakness. Four of five judges (all except qwen) flagged the rim-as-base/grip error as a factual problem, while qwen treated it as minor interpretive liberty. Judges split sharply on persuasion quality (4 to 9) depending on how much weight they gave unsupported performance guarantees, and on factual fidelity (4 to 8) depending on whether the omitted care/safety content was treated as lost or as still standing from Turn 1. Readability was the most consistent criterion, ranging only from 6 to 8.
